name: Comparative Structure Evaluation
description: Examines the frequency, symmetry, and forced rhetorical balance of comparative and superlative constructions.
mechanism: When tasked with evaluating options, providing product reviews, or writing essays, large language models inherently generate highly balanced, symmetrical, and stubbornly neutral comparative structures (e.g., 'On one hand X is Y, but on the other hand Z is W'). Because of rigid Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) designed to maximize harmlessness and neutrality, LLMs rely extraordinarily heavily on formal, non-committal transitional comparatives ('moreover', 'whereas', 'conversely', 'while some argue'). Conversely, genuine human comparison is frequently unbalanced, highly opinionated, structurally asymmetrical, and uses far fewer formal textbook markers. This syntactic extraction tool parses the dependency tree to identify the mathematical overuse of these formal, perfectly balanced comparative blocks, effectively scoring the text's alignment with sterilized AI 'pros and cons' drafting templates.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated product reviews, buying guides, comparison articles, or argumentative essays that exhibit a mathematically forced, non-committal 'both-sides' neutrality.
strengths:
• Precision-targeted directly at the overly accommodating 'helpful assistant' persona fundamentally baked into modern commercial LLMs.
• Exclusively relies on syntactic parsing rather than a heavy semantic embedding space, making the pipeline extraordinarily fast and highly scalable.
• Brilliantly identifies the 'forced neutrality' and rhetorical sterilization inherent in RLHF safety training.
limitations:
• A highly specialized metric that strongly applies only to evaluative, review-based, or argumentative texts; it is statistically useless on narrative fiction or poetry.
• Can trigger false positives on human text written specifically for strict diplomatic, academic, or corporate communication where forced neutrality is mandated.
• Can be bypassed by an experienced prompter explicitly commanding the AI to abandon neutrality and adopt a highly biased, unnuanced, or aggressive stance.
parameters:
Analysis: Syntactic Template & Dependency Tree Matching
Metric: Comparative Clause Density & Rhetorical Symmetry
Output: 0-100 Rhetorical Balance (Forced Neutrality) Score
accuracy: High — 80-85% when applied exclusively to evaluative, comparative, or review-based texts. Ineffective outside this domain.

references.title: Jurafsky, D. & Martin, J.H. (2024). Speech and Language Processing. 3rd Edition.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
